https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DXqXmz0YwQs

I'm not an HVAC guru, but I did have something similar happen once. It turned out a relay on my control board was bad. It could also be possible for the high speed input on the blower not to work, but for the lower speed setting to still be good. (This is assuming the motor has different speed settings, which is typical. AC uses high speed and heat uses lower speed.)

You can A) test the motor by removing the wire that goes from the safety switch on the furnace door to the control board and instead connecting that directly to the high speed input to the motor, or, if you prefer, you can B) switch the blower motor wires that connect to the AC and heat relays on the control board. Obviously turn off the power before doing either of these. Option A will turn the blower on all the time, and actually the AC doesn't depend on the control board, so this can serve as a work-around while you wait for a replacement board if that turns out to be the problem. Just don't leave it that way for a long time, because it's inefficient to run the blower all the time, and you'll need the control board working properly when it's time for heat again.

If you do this and the blower still doesn't run, or if you use option B and the blower only works with AC but not heat, you'll need a new motor. Don't try to run the AC with the lower speed setting of the motor, it won't work right. AC requires the high speed.
